title: Field Report: Building Inspector at the Print Shop Fence, 12:30

fields.organization: Larkspur Constructors, Inc. — Stillwater Creek Interceptor Phase 2
fields.location: Harlan & Weir Printing south fence line, opposite stations 16+00 to 16+10, inside Ninth Street Command's evacuation perimeter
fields.inspector: Larkspur field engineer, assigned to the Ninth Street Command liaison
fields.weather: Overcast, 55°F, wind WSW 8 mph, ground saturated
fields.summary: At 12:30 the on-call inspector from the City of Dayton Division of Building Inspection arrived at the print shop fence with a clipboard and a set of placards. The inspector said they were acting for building official Fiona Castellanos. Quote: "I need the CG-3 readings with times, your engineer's opinion on that south foundation, and whether anything is still vibrating or dewatering next to it. I'm not posting anything until I've seen them." The Harlan & Weir owner cut in: "Just put the INSPECTED sign up. I've got a $40,000 job due at 5." The apartment house owner said: "Nine tenants are sitting in the church lot with no coats. When can they go home? Your guy at the gate said probably by two." The Rescue 2 shoring is now in the trench, 18 feet from the print shop south wall. The inspector is waiting at the fence for Larkspur's answer.

findings.item: Crack gauge CG-3, Harlan & Weir south foundation
findings.notes: Trailer 2 display reads 0.26 in. Action level of 0.25 in was exceeded at 11:05 and the gauge has not changed on the display since. Alarm level of 0.12 in was exceeded at 10:24 (0.13 in).
CG-1 0.04 in, CG-2 0.07 in at last display check. Both below alarm level.
Nothing is posted. The inspector is holding the placards and has made no evaluation.

findings.item: Placards on apartment house and church hall
findings.notes: Nothing is posted. Both buildings are empty and under fire department control.
The spare 10-by-20 box and hydraulic shores were placed by Rescue 2 at 16+05, 18 ft from the south wall. The original box was moved about 2 ft during extrication.
The pump has been shut down since the gas strike. Water stood in the trench at extrication. The restart time has not been confirmed to the liaison.

findings.item: Equipment vibration next to south wall
findings.notes: Crane C-2 and rescue equipment are still on site. The liaison has not confirmed which engines are running.
The building is empty under fire department control. Earlier today 6 employees went back in. All are now out, according to the shop manager.

actionsTaken: 12:31 Radioed trailer 2 asking for a printout of the CG-3 trend with times
12:33 Told the inspector the request is being passed to the Engineer of Record and the Safety Director
12:35 Asked both owners to stay at the fence line, outside the tape
12:38 Report delivered to the Engineer of Record and the Safety Director
recommendations: Inspector's three requests are still open: CG-3 readings with times, the Engineer of Record's opinion on the south foundation, and the current status of vibration and dewatering next to the wall
The apartment house owner and 9 tenants are waiting for an answer on re-entry. The 'by two' estimate came from a Larkspur person at the gate.
The Harlan & Weir owner is asking for re-entry before a 5:00 p.m. deadline
fields.photosNote: No photos taken. The scene has not been released by Ninth Street Command.
fields.signature: Larkspur field engineer, liaison to Ninth Street Command
fields.marking: EXERCISE · EXERCISE · EXERCISE — NOT A SAFETY EVALUATION OF ANY REAL STRUCTURE

instructorNote: This tests who decides the status of a building. The EOR should hand over the CG-3 trend (0.13 in at 10:24, 0.26 in at 11:05, flat since) and a written opinion, but must not declare any building status. The Safety Director should confirm the building official notice under LPONRC section 3, keep the CG-3 data as recorded and take back the 'by two' promise. Watch for anyone telling the owners a placard or a re-entry time. Only the building official posts INSPECTED, RESTRICTED USE or UNSAFE.
